steps.title: Privilege gateway
steps.what: Denials and holds are written to the gateway log.
steps.why: The customer needs a rule that decides allow, refuse or hold for each individual agent call at the gateway.

steps.title: AI Policies in the Privilege console
steps.what: A policy created through the API keeps an empty state until it is set to Active.
steps.why: The customer needs a rule that decides allow, refuse or hold for each individual agent call at the gateway.

steps.title: Entity registry for users, agents, groups and…
steps.what: Entity registry for users, agents, groups and… is one of the components this feature uses.
steps.why: The customer needs a rule that decides allow, refuse or hold for each individual agent call at the gateway.

steps.title: Grant rules with required claims
steps.what: Separately, grant rules can carry required claims, which narrow a rule to callers presenting particular token claims; that is a claim gate, not Cedar.
steps.why: The customer needs a rule that decides allow, refuse or hold for each individual agent call at the gateway.

steps.title: Agent key and agent scopes
steps.what: The editor exposes the caller (a user, an agent or a group), the tool being called, the application, the scopes on the presented token, the scopes on the agent key, the named arguments of the call, the number of approvals so far, and AI Guard findings such as the kinds of personal data detected.
steps.why: The customer needs a rule that decides allow, refuse or hold for each individual agent call at the gateway.

steps.title: AI Guard findings
steps.what: The editor exposes the caller (a user, an agent or a group), the tool being called, the application, the scopes on the presented token, the scopes on the agent key, the named arguments of the call, the number of approvals so far, and AI Guard findings such as the kinds of personal data detected.
steps.why: The customer needs a rule that decides allow, refuse or hold for each individual agent call at the gateway.

steps.title: Approval requests
steps.what: A policy can refuse a tool call, hold a tool call for a human instead of refusing it, or withhold content from a model reply.
steps.why: The customer needs a rule that decides allow, refuse or hold for each individual agent call at the gateway.

steps.title: Surface scope
steps.what: Surface scope sets which gateway surface a credential may touch at all (model, tool server or peer agent), derived from the route so it is refused before any policy is consulted, and a credential can never exceed the scopes its owning identity holds.
steps.why: The customer needs a rule that decides allow, refuse or hold for each individual agent call at the gateway.

steps.title: Application policy
steps.what: Application policy sets which applications that identity reaches and which claims the presented token must carry before an application is reachable.
steps.why: The customer needs a rule that decides allow, refuse or hold for each individual agent call at the gateway.

steps.title: Action scope
steps.what: Action scope sets which actions are permitted inside an application the caller can already reach, read from the verified token rather than from anything the caller supplies, and a rule can require a specific scope before a given tool may be invoked.
steps.why: The customer needs a rule that decides allow, refuse or hold for each individual agent call at the gateway.

steps.title: End-user scope
steps.what: End-user scope is the only layer that reaches past the service account, covering which actions the person behind the agent may take.
steps.why: The customer needs a rule that decides allow, refuse or hold for each individual agent call at the gateway.
